- When sentiment is predominantly positive (≥ 0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for the next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.3) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–4% for the next 3–7 days.
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak for 2–4 days.
- If model forecast is consistently below true outcome over 3+ consecutive days, apply mean reversion: add 0.5–1.5x the recent 5-day average deviation to next forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows strong upward trend (e.g., > 2% avg daily gain), model often lags; shift forecast up by 0.5–1.5% per day for next 5–7 days.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive within 3 days, model often misses the momentum; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.
